```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())
```

## Overview

This script prepares grappe-level mortality data for the AVENIR spatial average treatment effect (ATE) analysis. The pipeline:

1. Loads GPS coordinates, phase-level mortality counts, and Niger administrative shapefiles.
2. Collapses phase-level records to a single row per grappe, summing person-years and deaths.
3. Joins spatial coordinates and recodes treatment labels.
4. Filters to the primary analysis cohort (Randomization 1).
5. Computes district-level mean mortality rates by treatment arm and their difference (ATE).
6. Saves processed data and a prediction grid for downstream spatial modeling.

---

### Configure environment. Load data.
```{r config and load data, warning=F}

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))

# GPS coordinates for each grappe (cluster); median lat/lon across households
d_gps <-
  read_csv(here(final_data,"AVENIR_grappe_gps_2023-07-31.csv")) %>%
  rename(lat = median_latitude,
         lon = median_longitude)

# Phase-level mortality data: one row per grappe × study phase
grappe_phase_mort <-
  readRDS(paste0(final_data,"AVENIR_grappe_phase_2023-07-31.rds"))

# Load Niger boundaries map from Humanitarian Data Exchange
# Map downloaded from https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ner on 10 March 2026

niger_adm1 <- st_read(dsn = here("data", "untouched", "ner_admin_boundaries", "ner_admin1.shp"))
niger_adm2 <- st_read(dsn = here("data", "untouched", "ner_admin_boundaries", "ner_admin2.shp"))

```

---

### Collapse phase-level data to grappe level

Each grappe has multiple rows in `grappe_phase_mort` (one per study phase). We sum person-years and deaths across all phases to obtain a single mortality rate per grappe over the full follow-up period. Mortality rates (deaths per 1,000 person-years) are computed directly within the same `summarise()` call after the sums are available.

Note: `started_phase_*` and `n_alive_*` columns are excluded — they cannot be meaningfully summed across phases and are not needed once we have total person-years.

```{r aggregate phase specific data}

# Dropping columns on started phase and n alive since they can't be summed across phases. We also don't need them to calculate mortality rates since we have person-years.

grappe_mort <-
  grappe_phase_mort %>%
  group_by(region, district, site_code, grappe, adaptive_rand, tx) %>%
  summarise(
    # started_phase_1to59 = sum(started_phase_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    pt_year_1to59 = sum(pt_year_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    # n_alive_1to59 = sum(n_alive_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_1to59 = sum(lost_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),

    # started_phase_1to11 = sum(started_phase_1to11, na.rm = TRUE),
    pt_year_1to11 = sum(pt_year_1to11, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_deaths_1to11 = sum(n_deaths_1to11, na.rm = TRUE),
    # n_alive_1to11 = sum(n_alive_1to11, na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_1to11 = sum(lost_1to11, na.rm = TRUE),

    # started_phase_12to59 = sum(started_phase_12to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    pt_year_12to59 = sum(pt_year_12to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_deaths_12to59 = sum(n_deaths_12to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    # n_alive_12to59 = sum(n_alive_12to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_12to59 = sum(lost_12to59, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Mortality rates computed within summarise() after summing — valid in dplyr >= 1.1
    deaths_per_1000_1to59 = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
    deaths_per_1000_1to11 = n_deaths_1to11 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to11,
    deaths_per_1000_12to59 = n_deaths_12to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_12to59
  )

# grappe_mort

# Verify expected number of unique sites
length(unique(grappe_phase_mort$site_code))

```

---

### Join GPS coordinates to outcome data

Grappe-level GPS coordinates (latitude, longitude, and CSI health facility code) are joined to the mortality data by `site_code`. This provides the spatial locations needed for all subsequent geostatistical modeling.

```{r add gps to data}
d_gps_latlon <- d_gps %>%
  dplyr::select(site_code, lat, lon, csi)

grappe_mort <- grappe_mort %>%
  left_join(d_gps_latlon, by = "site_code") %>%
  relocate(c(lat, lon), .after = grappe)

```

---

### Harmonize district names with shapefile

Two district names in the outcome data differ from those in the Niger ADM2 shapefile. These are corrected here so that downstream spatial joins and map labels match correctly.

```{r rename districts to match shapefile district names}

grappe_mort <- grappe_mort %>%
  mutate(district = case_when(
    district == "Tibiri (Doutchi)" ~ "Tibiri",  # shapefile uses just "Tibiri"
    district == "Illela"           ~ "Illéla",  # restore accented form used in shapefile
    .default = district
  ))
```

---

### Recode treatment labels and create analysis indicators

Treatment arms are relabeled to match manuscript nomenclature. Two binary treatment indicators are created:

- `isTreated_child`: Treatment = "Child Azithro" only (primary analysis arm); all others are Control.
- `isTreated_alltx`: Treatment = either azithromycin arm; Placebo = Control.

The adaptive randomization label is also shortened to "Randomization 1/2/3". A `dummy` column (always 1) is added as a constant covariate required by the spaMM model formula.

The data is then filtered to **Randomization 1 only**, which is the primary pre-specified analysis cohort. Grappes from Randomizations 2 and 3 are retained in a separate unfiltered object for descriptive figures.

```{r add tx labels and indicators}

# Recode tx labels to align with ms nomenclature
grappe_mort <- grappe_mort %>%
  mutate(
    tx = case_when(
      tx == "1 - Azithro 1-59m" ~ "Child Azithro",
      tx == "2 - Azithro 1-11m" ~ "Infant Azithro",
      tx == "3 - Placebo 1-59m" ~ "Placebo"),

    # Primary analysis: "Child Azithro" vs. all others
    isTreated_child = case_when(
      tx == "Child Azithro" ~ "Treatment",
      .default = "Control"
    ),

    # Secondary analysis: any azithromycin arm vs. placebo
    isTreated_alltx = case_when(
      tx == "Placebo" ~ "Control",
      .default = "Treatment"
    ),

    tx              = factor(tx,              levels = c("Child Azithro", "Infant Azithro", "Placebo")),
    isTreated_child = factor(isTreated_child, levels = c("Control", "Treatment")),
    isTreated_alltx = factor(isTreated_alltx, levels = c("Control", "Treatment")),

    # shorten adaptive randomization labels
    adaptive_rand = factor(adaptive_rand,
                           levels = c("Random Allocation 1",
                                      "Random Allocation 2",
                                      "Random Allocation 3"),
                           labels = c("Randomization 1",
                                      "Randomization 2",
                                      "Randomization 3")),
    # constant covariate required by spaMM model formula
    dummy = 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Filter to Randomization 1 (primary analysis cohort)
grappe_mort_filt <- grappe_mort %>%
  filter(adaptive_rand == "Randomization 1")

# Verify treatment × arm counts
grappe_mort_filt %>% group_by(tx, isTreated_child) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
# df_all %>% group_by(tx, isTreated_alltx) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Verify treatment balance across districts
grappe_mort_filt %>% group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
# df_all %>% group_by(district, isTreated_alltx) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

```

---

### Compute district-level mean mortality rates and ATE

For descriptive purposes, we compute mean mortality rates by district and treatment arm, then take their difference as a naive district-level ATE estimate. This is used for mapping and summary tables, not for the primary inference.

```{r add district level ATE by treatment group}

set.seed(42)
n_boot <- 10000

districts <- unique(grappe_mort_filt$district)

boot_ates <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(n_boot), function(i) {
  boot_data <- purrr::map_dfr(districts, function(d) {
    d_dat <- grappe_mort_filt %>% dplyr::filter(district == d)
    d_dat[sample(nrow(d_dat), size = nrow(d_dat), replace = TRUE), ]
  })

  # District-level ATEs
  district_rows <- boot_data %>%
    group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>%
    summarise(
      n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
      pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59,  na.rm = TRUE),
      MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
      .groups        = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = isTreated_child,
      values_from = c(n_deaths_1to59, pt_year_1to59, MortRate)
    ) %>%
    mutate(ATE = MortRate_Treatment - MortRate_Control) %>%
    dplyr::select(district, ATE)

  # Overall pooled-rate ATE (PY-weighted across all districts)
  overall_row <- boot_data %>%
    group_by(isTreated_child) %>%
    summarise(
      n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
      pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59,  na.rm = TRUE),
      MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
      .groups        = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = isTreated_child,
      values_from = c(n_deaths_1to59, pt_year_1to59, MortRate)
    ) %>%
    mutate(district = "Overall", ATE = MortRate_Treatment - MortRate_Control) %>%
    dplyr::select(district, ATE)

  bind_rows(district_rows, overall_row)
}, mc.cores = avail_thr)

boot_ates_df <- purrr::map_dfr(boot_ates, identity, .id = "replicate")

dist_ate_summ <- grappe_mort_filt %>%
  group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
            pt_year_1to59 = sum(pt_year_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
            MortRate = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = isTreated_child,
              values_from = c(n, n_deaths_1to59, pt_year_1to59, MortRate)) %>%
  # ATE = simple difference in mean mortality rates (Treatment − Control)
  mutate(ATE = MortRate_Treatment - MortRate_Control)

# Observed overall pooled estimate
overall_ate_obs <- grappe_mort_filt %>%
  group_by(isTreated_child) %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = isTreated_child,
              values_from = c(n, n_deaths_1to59, pt_year_1to59, MortRate)) %>%
  mutate(district = "Overall", ATE = MortRate_Treatment - MortRate_Control)

dist_ate_summ <- bind_rows(dist_ate_summ, overall_ate_obs)

dist_ate_summ <- dist_ate_summ %>%
  left_join(
    boot_ates_df %>%
      group_by(district) %>%
      summarise(
        ATE_mean    = mean(ATE, na.rm = TRUE),
        ATE_CI_low  = quantile(ATE, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
        ATE_CI_high = quantile(ATE, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "district"
  ) %>%
  mutate(ATE_CI = paste0(round(ATE, 2), " (95% CI: ", round(ATE_CI_low, 2), " to ", round(ATE_CI_high, 2), ")"))

```

```{r add district level mortality by treatment group}

boot_mort_tx <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(n_boot), function(i) {
  boot_data <- purrr::map_dfr(districts, function(d) {
    d_dat <- grappe_mort_filt %>% dplyr::filter(district == d)
    d_dat[sample(nrow(d_dat), size = nrow(d_dat), replace = TRUE), ]
  })
  
  district_rows <- boot_data %>%
    group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>%
    summarise(
      n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
      pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59,  na.rm = TRUE),
      MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
      .groups        = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(district, MortRate, isTreated_child)
  
  overall_row <- boot_data %>%
    group_by(isTreated_child) %>%
    summarise(
      n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
      pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59,  na.rm = TRUE),
      MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
      .groups        = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(district = "Overall") %>%
    dplyr::select(district, MortRate, isTreated_child)
  
  bind_rows(district_rows, overall_row)
  
}, mc.cores = avail_thr)

boot_mort_tx_df <- purrr::map_dfr(boot_mort_tx, identity, .id = "replicate") %>%
      group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>%
      summarise(
        MortRate_mean    = mean(MortRate, na.rm = TRUE),
        MortRate_CI_low  = quantile(MortRate, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
        MortRate_CI_high = quantile(MortRate, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

overall_mort_tx_obs <- grappe_mort_filt %>%
  group_by(isTreated_child) %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    pt_year_1to59  = sum(pt_year_1to59,  na.rm = TRUE),
    MortRate       = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(district = "Overall")

dist_tx_summ <- grappe_mort_filt %>%
  group_by(district, isTreated_child) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
            pt_year_1to59 = sum(pt_year_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
            MortRate = n_deaths_1to59 * 1e3 / pt_year_1to59,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  bind_rows(overall_mort_tx_obs) %>%
  left_join(
    boot_mort_tx_df,
    by = c("district", "isTreated_child")
  ) %>%
  mutate(MortRate_CI = paste0(round(MortRate, 2), " (95% CI: ", round(MortRate_CI_low, 2), " to ", round(MortRate_CI_high, 2), ")"))

```

---

### Save processed data

Three objects are saved:

- `grappe_mortality_data.rds` — Randomization 1 cohort; used in all primary analyses.
- `district_mortality_means.rds` — District-level mean mortality rates and naive ATE estimates.
- `grappe_mortality_data_all_rands.rds` — Full data across all randomizations; used in Figure 1.

```{r save data}

saveRDS(grappe_mort_filt, here("data", "grappe_mortality_data.rds"))

saveRDS(dist_ate_summ, here("data", "district_ATE_means.rds"))

saveRDS(dist_tx_summ, here("data", "district_mortality_means_by_treatment_group.rds"))
saveRDS(dist_rand_summ, here("data", "district_mortality_means_by_randomization_arm.rds"))

# Save data not filtered for randomization 1 for figure 1
saveRDS(grappe_mort, here("data", "grappe_mortality_data_all_rands.rds"))

```

---

### Build and save spatial prediction grid

A regular grid of prediction locations (centroids) is constructed over the study area for use in spatial interpolation. The grid is:

1. Built over the bounding box of the study districts at resolution `grid_res` × `grid_res` (set in `0-config.R`).
2. Clipped to the district boundaries so predictions are only generated inside the study area.

Both the district polygon subset and the clipped grid are saved for use in the modeling and mapping scripts.

```{r save cropped mapping data}

districts <- unique(grappe_mort_filt$district)

# Inspect CRS of downloaded shapefile before transforming
crs(niger_adm2)

# Subset to study districts only; st_make_valid() repairs any self-intersecting
# polygon geometries that can cause downstream spatial operations to fail
niger_adm2_sub <- niger_adm2 %>%
  filter(adm2_name %in% districts) %>%
  st_make_valid()

niger_adm2_sub_proj <- niger_adm2_sub %>%
  st_transform(crs = proj_crs)

# Build a regular grid of point centroids over the study area bounding box,
# then clip to district boundaries so only interior points are retained
b_boxgrid <- st_make_grid(
  niger_adm2_sub_proj,
  n = c(grid_res, grid_res),  # grid_res defined in 0-config.R
  what = "centers",
  crs = proj_crs
) %>%
  st_sf(geometry = .) %>%
  st_filter(niger_adm2_sub_proj)  # drop points outside study districts

saveRDS(niger_adm2_sub, here("data", "niger_adm2_sub.rds"))
saveRDS(b_boxgrid, here("data", "boxgrid.rds"))

```
